components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads, as in 道 road, 过 pass, 进 enter.
巛 (川 chuān, river) is a loose sound clue; 训 xùn and 顺 shùn share it.
辶 (walk) — patrolling on the move; also in 道 road, 过 pass.
罗 (luó) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 萝 luó and 锣 luó.

example.hanzi: 警察每晚都会在这条街上巡逻。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá měi wǎn dōu huì zài zhè tiáo jiē shàng xúnluó.
example.english: Police patrol this street every night.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China was never a single continuous structure but a network of walls, watchtowers, and beacon towers built and rebuilt by different dynasties over roughly two thousand years, and Ming-era garrisons used smoke and fire signals from tower to tower to relay warnings of approaching threats faster than any rider could travel.

examples.hanzi: 保安每小时在小区里巡逻一次。
examples.pinyin: Bǎo'ān měi xiǎoshí zài xiǎoqū lǐ xúnluó yí cì.
examples.english: The security guard patrols the neighborhood once an hour.

examples.hanzi: 海边有救生员巡逻。
examples.pinyin: Hǎibiān yǒu jiùshēngyuán xúnluó.
examples.english: Lifeguards patrol the beach.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.

example.hanzi: 花园角落里有一片小小的菜地。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán jiǎoluò lǐ yǒu yí piàn xiǎoxiǎo de càidì.
example.english: There's a tiny vegetable patch in the corner of the garden.
example.fact: Tardigrades, microscopic animals often called 'water bears,' can survive in a dried-out state for over a decade and endure conditions that would kill nearly any other animal, including the vacuum of space — several species were sent into low Earth orbit in 2007 and survived direct solar radiation exposure.

examples.hanzi: 小小的房间里放着一张床。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxiǎo de fángjiān lǐ fàngzhe yì zhāng chuáng.
examples.english: A small bed sits in the tiny room.

examples.hanzi: 别看他年纪小小的，懂的可多了。
examples.pinyin: Bié kàn tā niánjì xiǎoxiǎo de, dǒng de kě duō le.
examples.english: Though he's little, he knows a lot.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 呼, 吃, 喝; 吸 is to breathe in.
及 (jí) is a loose sound hint for xī; same part in 级 jí and 极 jí.
火 (fire) — 火 is fire, as in 烧, 灯, 炒; 烟 is smoke.
因 (yīn) — near sound — 烟 is yān; 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn.

example.hanzi: 医院里到处都写着禁止吸烟。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn lǐ dàochù dōu xiězhe jìnzhǐ xīyān.
example.english: Signs banning smoking are posted everywhere in the hospital.
example.fact: The link between smoking and lung cancer was firmly established by large epidemiological studies in the early 1950s, notably by Richard Doll and Austin Bradford Hill in the UK, whose research tracking thousands of British doctors provided some of the first solid statistical evidence connecting the habit to the disease.

examples.hanzi: 公共场所不允许吸烟。
examples.pinyin: Gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ bù yǔnxǔ xīyān.
examples.english: Smoking is not allowed in public places.

examples.hanzi: 医生劝他不要再吸烟了。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng quàn tā bú yào zài xīyān le.
examples.english: The doctor advised him to stop smoking.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
衣 (clothing) — cloth ripping apart; also as 衤 in 衬, 被.
列 (liè) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 烈 liè.

example.hanzi: 这个组织内部出现了严重分裂。
example.pinyin: Zhège zǔzhī nèibù chūxiàn le yánzhòng fēnliè.
example.english: A serious split emerged within this organization.
example.fact: Nuclear fission, the splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus into smaller fragments, was first experimentally demonstrated in 1938 by Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann, with Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch providing the theoretical explanation shortly after — a discovery that release enormous energy and set the stage for both nuclear power and nuclear weapons.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家分裂成了两个部分。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā fēnliè chéng le liǎng ge bùfen.
examples.english: This country split into two parts.

examples.hanzi: 细胞会不断分裂和生长。
examples.pinyin: Xìbāo huì búduàn fēnliè hé shēngzhǎng.
examples.english: Cells keep dividing and growing.

meanings: notebook (abbr. for 筆記本電腦|笔记本电脑[bi3 ji4 ben3 dian4 nao3])

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — brush shafts were bamboo; also in 笑 smile, 筷 chopsticks.
毛 (hair) — the brush hair at the tip; 笔 is brush and pen.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.
木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.

example.hanzi: 他把资料存在了笔记本电脑里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zīliào cún zài le bǐjìběn diànnǎo lǐ.
example.english: He saved the files on his laptop.
example.fact: The first commercially successful laptop, the Osborne 1, was released in 1981, weighed about 11 kilograms, and had a screen barely five inches wide — yet it was considered revolutionary for being 'portable' at all, since most computers at the time filled entire rooms or desks.

examples.hanzi: 上课时我用笔记本记笔记。
examples.pinyin: Shàngkè shí wǒ yòng bǐjìběn jì bǐjì.
examples.english: In class I take notes in my notebook.

examples.hanzi: 这台笔记本很轻，方便带出门。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái bǐjìběn hěn qīng, fāngbiàn dài chūmén.
examples.english: This laptop is light and easy to take out.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 香 originally combined grain with 甘 (sweet): the smell of cooked grain, in modern writing 日 stands in for 甘.
艹 (grass) — plants; 蕉 is the banana plant, as in 花 flower, 草 grass.
焦 (jiāo) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 礁 jiāo.

example.hanzi: 猴子最爱吃的水果就是香蕉。
example.pinyin: Hóuzi zuì ài chī de shuǐguǒ jiùshì xiāngjiāo.
example.english: The fruit monkeys love most is bananas.
example.fact: Nearly all commercially grown bananas belong to a single cultivar called the Cavendish, propagated by cloning rather than seed, which makes the entire global supply genetically identical and highly vulnerable to disease — a fungal outbreak called Panama disease has already wiped out the previous dominant variety, the Gros Michel, in the mid-20th century.

examples.hanzi: 我早餐喜欢吃一根香蕉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǎocān xǐhuan chī yì gēn xiāngjiāo.
examples.english: I like eating a banana for breakfast.

examples.hanzi: 这串香蕉还没熟。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chuàn xiāngjiāo hái méi shú.
examples.english: This bunch of bananas isn't ripe yet.

components.note: 车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.
宀 (roof) — a public building where officials work; 官 is an official.
官 (guān) gives the sound of 管 guǎn, 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 他是一位受人尊敬的军官。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi shòu rén zūnjìng de jūnguān.
example.english: He is a well-respected military officer.
example.fact: The Enigma machine used by German military officers in World War II was considered virtually unbreakable, yet a team at Bletchley Park led by mathematicians including Alan Turing built machines called 'bombes' that could crack its daily settings, an intelligence breakthrough historians credit with shortening the war significantly.

examples.hanzi: 那位军官正在检查士兵的装备。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi jūnguān zhèngzài jiǎnchá shìbīng de zhuāngbèi.
examples.english: That officer is inspecting the soldiers' equipment.

examples.hanzi: 我叔叔退休前是一名军官。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shūshu tuìxiū qián shì yì míng jūnguān.
examples.english: My uncle was an officer before he retired.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 他, 做; 侵 is to encroach, as in 入侵; the right side also sounds out 浸 jìn.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 敌军趁夜色侵入了边境村庄。
example.pinyin: Díjūn chèn yèsè qīnrù le biānjìng cūnzhuāng.
example.english: The enemy troops invaded the border village under cover of darkness.
example.fact: Cane toads were deliberately introduced to Australia in 1935 to control beetles damaging sugarcane crops, but the toads failed to eat the target pest and instead spread explosively across the continent, becoming one of the most notorious invasive species in modern ecological history.

examples.hanzi: 有人侵入了公司的电脑系统。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén qīnrù le gōngsī de diànnǎo xìtǒng.
examples.english: Someone broke into the company's computer system.

examples.hanzi: 暴风雨侵入了海边的小镇。
examples.pinyin: Bàofēngyǔ qīnrù le hǎibiān de xiǎozhèn.
examples.english: The storm swept into the seaside town.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person crouching low; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
犬 (dog) — a dog crouching beside a person is the old image for lying low.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 这个灯泡需要220伏特的电压。
example.pinyin: Zhège dēngpào xūyào èrbǎi'èrshí fútè de diànyā.
example.english: This light bulb requires a voltage of 220 volts.
example.fact: The volt is named after Alessandro Volta, the Italian physicist who invented the first true battery, the voltaic pile, in 1800 by stacking alternating discs of zinc and copper separated by brine-soaked cloth — the first device able to produce a steady, continuous electric current.

examples.hanzi: 普通家用电的电压是二百二十伏特。
examples.pinyin: Pǔtōng jiāyòng diàn de diànyā shì èrbǎi èrshí fútè.
examples.english: The voltage of ordinary household electricity is 220 volts.

examples.hanzi: 这块电池只有一点五伏特。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài diànchí zhǐyǒu yì diǎn wǔ fútè.
examples.english: This battery is only 1.5 volts.

components.note: 马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.
木 (wood) — buckets were wooden; also in 树 tree, 桌 table.
甬 (yǒng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 通 tōng, 痛 tòng and 勇 yǒng.

example.hanzi: 旧房子里还留着一个老式马桶。
example.pinyin: Jiù fángzi lǐ hái liú zhe yí gè lǎoshì mǎtǒng.
example.english: There's still an old-fashioned chamber pot left in the old house.
example.fact: Sir John Harington, godson of Queen Elizabeth I, designed an early flush toilet in 1596 and installed one for the queen at Richmond Palace, but the invention was largely ignored for nearly two centuries until Alexander Cumming patented an improved flush design in 1775.

examples.hanzi: 请记得冲马桶。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jìde chōng mǎtǒng.
examples.english: Please remember to flush the toilet.

examples.hanzi: 马桶坏了，要找人来修。
examples.pinyin: Mǎtǒng huài le, yào zhǎo rén lái xiū.
examples.english: The toilet is broken, so we need to get someone to fix it.

components.note: 小 (small) — a 小 with a stroke taken off: not much. 少 also gives sound to 沙 shā, 抄 chāo and 炒 chǎo.
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 他从少年时期就开始学习画画。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng shàonián shíqī jiù kāishǐ xuéxí huàhuà.
example.english: He started learning to paint from his teenage years.
example.fact: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart began composing music at the age of five and was touring European royal courts as a performing prodigy by age six, with his father chronicling and promoting his early talent across years of demanding travel.

examples.hanzi: 那个少年每天骑车去上学。
examples.pinyin: Nàge shàonián měi tiān qí chē qù shàngxué.
examples.english: That boy rides a bike to school every day.

examples.hanzi: 少年时期的他非常爱读书。
examples.pinyin: Shàonián shíqī de tā fēicháng ài dúshū.
examples.english: In his youth he loved reading very much.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — noise made by voices; also in 叫 shout, 吵 noisy.
喿 (zào) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 燥 zào, 澡 zǎo and 躁 zào.
音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.

example.hanzi: 工地传来的噪音吵得人睡不着。
example.pinyin: Gōngdì chuánlái de zàoyīn chǎo de rén shuìbùzháo.
example.english: The noise from the construction site was so loud that people couldn't sleep.
example.fact: Sound is measured on a logarithmic decibel scale, meaning every increase of 10 decibels represents a tenfold increase in sound intensity — a jet engine at close range, around 140 decibels, is roughly ten trillion times more intense than the quietest sound the human ear can detect.

examples.hanzi: 深夜的噪音让邻居很生气。
examples.pinyin: Shēnyè de zàoyīn ràng línjū hěn shēngqì.
examples.english: The late-night noise made the neighbors very angry.

examples.hanzi: 这台冰箱几乎没有噪音。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái bīngxiāng jīhū méiyǒu zàoyīn.
examples.english: This refrigerator makes almost no noise.

meanings: the only son of a family

components.note: 单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 他是家里的单子,爷爷奶奶特别宠他。
example.pinyin: Tā shì jiā lǐ de dānzǐ, yéye nǎinai tèbié chǒng tā.
example.english: He is the only son in the family, and his grandparents dote on him especially.
example.fact: China's one-child policy, enforced from 1980 to 2015, led to a generation sometimes called 'little emperors' — only children who, without siblings, often received concentrated parental and grandparental attention and resources, a demographic shift sociologists are still studying decades later.

examples.hanzi: 你把要买的东西写在单子上吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ yào mǎi de dōngxi xiě zài dānzǐ shàng ba.
examples.english: Write the things you need to buy on the list.

examples.hanzi: 我把新床单子铺好了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ xīn chuángdānzǐ pūhǎo le.
examples.english: I've put on the new bed sheet.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 日 is the sun — 暴 originally meant to expose to the sun (still in 暴露), then violent, as in 暴力.

example.hanzi: 昨天下了一场暴雨。
example.pinyin: Zuótiān xià le yì chǎng bàoyǔ.
example.english: There was a heavy rainstorm yesterday.
example.fact: 暴 means sudden and violent: 暴雨 (downpour), 暴力 (violence), 暴躁 (short-tempered), 暴富 (sudden wealth). The older meaning was exposing grain to the sun, now written 曝 (pù).

examples.hanzi: 他是个脾气暴躁的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge píqi bàozào de rén.
examples.english: He is a hot-tempered person.

examples.hanzi: 今天晚上有暴风雨。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang yǒu bàofēngyǔ.
examples.english: There will be a rainstorm tonight.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family: 妈, 姐, 奶, 姑; 婆 is an old woman or grandmother.
波 (bō) gives the sound (pó); same part in 坡 pō and 玻 bō.

example.hanzi: 我外婆住在乡下。
example.pinyin: Wǒ wàipó zhù zài xiāngxià.
example.english: My grandmother lives in the countryside.
example.fact: 婆 is bound: 外婆 (maternal grandmother), 婆婆 (husband's mother), 婆家 (the husband's family), 老婆 (colloquial "wife"). 婆婆妈妈 describes someone who nags or fusses.

examples.hanzi: 我婆婆今年六十岁了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ pópo jīnnián liùshí suì le.
examples.english: My mother-in-law is sixty this year.

examples.hanzi: 老婆婆在门口晒太阳。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo pópo zài ménkǒu shài tàiyáng.
examples.english: The old lady is sunning herself at the door.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 把 is to grasp.
巴 (bā) gives the sound: 把 bǎ is close, as in 爸 bà and 吧 ba.
戈 (halberd) — weapons, as in 战 war and 成; the traditional 戲 was a play or contest.

example.hanzi: 这只是魔术师的把戏,别被骗了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì móshùshī de bǎxì, bié bèi piàn le.
example.english: This is just the magician's trick, don't be fooled.
example.fact: Harry Houdini, one of history's most famous escape artists, died in 1926 not from a failed stunt but from a ruptured appendix, after a college student punched him in the stomach backstage to test a claim that Houdini could withstand any blow — he continued performing for days before the injury proved fatal.

examples.hanzi: 这些把戏骗不了我。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē bǎxì piàn bu liǎo wǒ.
examples.english: These tricks can't fool me.

examples.hanzi: 马戏团里有很多精彩的把戏。
examples.pinyin: Mǎxìtuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō jīngcǎi de bǎxì.
examples.english: The circus has many wonderful tricks.

components.note: 各 (each) — a foot 夂 arriving at a place 口: each one coming. 各 also sounds out 路 lù, 格 gé, 客 kè and 洛 luò.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 这种植物在各地都能生长。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zhíwù zài gèdì dōu néng shēngzhǎng.
example.english: This kind of plant can grow in all sorts of places.
example.fact: Dandelions are found on every continent except Antarctica and can reproduce through a process called apomixis, producing viable seeds without needing pollination at all — a trait that has helped the plant spread into an astonishing range of climates and soil types worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 游客从各地来到这座城市。
examples.pinyin: Yóukè cóng gèdì lái dào zhè zuò chéngshì.
examples.english: Tourists come to this city from all over.

examples.hanzi: 各地的人口味都不一样。
examples.pinyin: Gèdì de rén kǒuwèi dōu bù yíyàng.
examples.english: People's tastes differ from region to region.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go toward someone.
卬 (áng) is a loose sound clue for yíng; 卬 also in 仰 yǎng.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.

example.hanzi: 全家人都到机场迎接他回国。
example.pinyin: Quán jiā rén dōu dào jīchǎng yíngjiē tā huíguó.
example.english: The whole family went to the airport to welcome him home.
example.fact: When the Apollo 11 astronauts returned to Earth in 1969, they were quarantined for 21 days before their public welcome, as NASA — with no way to be sure moon dust was safe — took the precaution of isolating the crew in case they had brought back any unknown lunar microorganisms.

examples.hanzi: 新年到了，我们一起迎接新的一年。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián dào le, wǒmen yìqǐ yíngjiē xīn de yì nián.
examples.english: The New Year has arrived, so let's welcome it together.

examples.hanzi: 校长在门口迎接新同学。
examples.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng zài ménkǒu yíngjiē xīn tóngxué.
examples.english: The principal greets the new students at the gate.

components.note: 石 (stone) — stone and hardness, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 码 code: 确 is solid, certain.
角 (jiǎo) replaces 隺 (hè) of 確 and is only a loose clue for què.

example.hanzi: 你确定明天不下雨吗？
example.pinyin: Nǐ quèdìng míngtiān bú xià yǔ ma?
example.english: Are you sure it won't rain tomorrow?
example.fact: 确 appears in compounds for certainty: 确定 (to be sure), 确实 (indeed), 正确 (correct), 准确 (accurate), 明确 (clear), 确认 (to confirm), 确诊 (confirmed diagnosis).

examples.hanzi: 这个消息很准确。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi hěn zhǔnquè.
examples.english: This news is very accurate.

examples.hanzi: 我不确定他今天来不来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú quèdìng tā jīntiān lái bu lái.
examples.english: I am not sure whether he is coming today.

components.note: 兔 — a pictograph of a rabbit: long ears on top and a short dot of a tail; compare 免 without the dot.

example.hanzi: 兔子喜欢吃胡萝卜。
example.pinyin: Tùzi xǐhuan chī húluóbo.
example.english: Rabbits like to eat carrots.
example.fact: 兔 is the fourth animal of the Chinese zodiac. In Chinese folklore a jade rabbit (玉兔) lives on the Moon pounding the elixir of life, which is why Chang'e lunar probes carried a rover named Yutu. Rabbits are counted with 只.

examples.hanzi: 她养了一只白兔子。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǎng le yì zhī bái tùzi.
examples.english: She keeps a white rabbit.

examples.hanzi: 兔年出生的人属兔。
examples.pinyin: Tù nián chūshēng de rén shǔ tù.
examples.english: People born in the Year of the Rabbit are rabbits in the zodiac.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand; 扫 (simplified 掃) is a hand with a broom 帚, to sweep.

example.hanzi: 周末我在家打扫房间。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ zài jiā dǎsǎo fángjiān.
example.english: On weekends I clean the rooms at home.
example.fact: 扫 is to sweep: 扫地, 打扫 (to clean up), 扫描 (to scan). 扫码 (to scan a QR code) is part of daily payments in China, and 扫兴 means to dampen someone's mood. The noun broom, 扫帚, is read sàozhou.

examples.hanzi: 他每天早上扫地。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang sǎodì.
examples.english: He sweeps the floor every morning.

examples.hanzi: 请扫一下这个二维码。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng sǎo yíxià zhège èrwéimǎ.
examples.english: Please scan this QR code.

components.note: 犭 (dog, beast) — animals: 狗, 猫, 狼; 独 first meant a solitary animal, then alone.
The old sound part 蜀 (shǔ) is also in 属 shǔ, 烛 zhú and 触 chù; simplified 独 shows 虫 instead.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢独自旅行。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan dúzì lǚxíng.
example.english: He likes to travel alone.
example.fact: 独 appears in 独立 (independent), 独特 (unique), 独自 (by oneself), 独生子女 (only child). It differs from 孤独 (lonely), which is about the feeling; 独 is mostly about being single or sole.

examples.hanzi: 他一个人独自住在山里。
examples.pinyin: Tā yí ge rén dúzì zhù zài shān lǐ.
examples.english: He lives alone in the mountains.

examples.hanzi: 她是家里的独生女。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì jiālǐ de dúshēngnǚ.
examples.english: She is the only daughter in her family.

components.note: 罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and catching: 罗, 罚, 罪; 置 first meant to set a net, then to place.
直 (zhí) is a near sound match for zhì; same part in 值 zhí and 植 zhí.

example.hanzi: 请告诉我你的位置。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de wèizhi.
example.english: Please tell me where you are.
example.fact: 置 means to place: 位置 (position), 设置 (settings), 装置 (device), 购置 (to purchase), 闲置 (idle). In chat apps, 置顶 means to pin a conversation to the top.

examples.hanzi: 他把书放置在桌子上。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ shū fàngzhì zài zhuōzi shàng.
examples.english: He placed the book on the table.

examples.hanzi: 我们新买了一套家具，布置得很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xīn mǎi le yí tào jiājù, bùzhì de hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: We bought a new set of furniture and arranged it beautifully.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 他手头现在有点紧,想借点钱。
example.pinyin: Tā shǒutóu xiànzài yǒudiǎn jǐn, xiǎng jiè diǎn qián.
example.english: He's a bit short on cash right now and wants to borrow some money.
example.fact: Before paper money existed, several ancient societies used commodity currencies with intrinsic value, including cacao beans in Mesoamerica and salt in parts of Africa and Rome — the word 'salary' itself is often traced to the Latin word for salt, reflecting how directly people once linked pay to physical goods.

examples.hanzi: 这个月手头有点紧，先不买了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè shǒutóu yǒudiǎn jǐn, xiān bù mǎi le.
examples.english: Money is tight this month, so I won't buy it for now.

examples.hanzi: 我手头没有带笔，你有吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shǒutóu méiyǒu dài bǐ, nǐ yǒu ma?
examples.english: I don't have a pen on hand, do you?

components.note: 页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
疒 (illness, 病字旁) — illness and pain: 病 ill, 疼 ache, 瘦 thin, 疯 mad; 痛 is pain.
甬 (yǒng) is a loose sound clue; same part in 通 tōng and 桶 tǒng.

example.hanzi: 他昨天喝多了酒,今天头痛得厉害。
example.pinyin: Tā zuótiān hē duō le jiǔ, jīntiān tóutòng de lìhài.
example.english: He drank too much yesterday and has a terrible headache today.
example.fact: Migraines are increasingly understood to involve waves of altered electrical activity spreading across the brain's surface, called cortical spreading depression, which researchers believe can trigger the visual disturbances, known as auras, that some migraine sufferers experience before the pain even begins.

examples.hanzi: 我头痛，想早点休息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tóutòng, xiǎng zǎodiǎn xiūxi.
examples.english: I have a headache and want to rest early.

examples.hanzi: 他经常头痛，应该去看医生。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngcháng tóutòng, yīnggāi qù kàn yīshēng.
examples.english: He often has headaches and should see a doctor.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — creatures, as in 蛇 snake, 蚊 mosquito.
胡 (hú) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 湖 hú, 糊 hú and 葫 hú.
虫 (insect) — creatures, as in 蛇 snake, 蚊 mosquito.
枼 (yè) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 碟 dié and 谍 dié.

example.hanzi: 花园里飞来了一只漂亮的蝴蝶。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ fēi lái le yì zhī piàoliang de húdié.
example.english: A beautiful butterfly flew into the garden.
example.fact: Monarch butterflies migrate up to 4,800 kilometers between Canada and central Mexico each year, yet no single butterfly completes the round trip — the journey takes multiple generations, with each one somehow inheriting the route information needed to continue it, a phenomenon still not fully understood by biologists.

examples.hanzi: 蝴蝶落在花朵上。
examples.pinyin: Húdié luò zài huāduǒ shàng.
examples.english: A butterfly landed on the flower.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们追着蝴蝶跑。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zhuīzhe húdié pǎo.
examples.english: The kids ran chasing the butterfly.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — retching through the mouth; also in 吐 vomit, 叫 shout.
区 (qū) is a loose clue; 欧 ōu shares it and sounds nearly like 呕 ǒu.
口 (mouth) — spitting out; also in 叫 shout, 吃 eat.
土 (tǔ) gives the exact sound (tǔ), also read tù as in 呕吐.

example.hanzi: 她晕车晕得厉害,一路都在呕吐。
example.pinyin: Tā yùnchē yùn de lìhài, yílù dōu zài ǒutù.
example.english: She got badly carsick and was vomiting the whole way.
example.fact: Motion sickness is thought to arise from a mismatch between what the inner ear senses about movement and what the eyes perceive, a conflict some scientists suspect the brain interprets as a possible sign of poisoning, triggering nausea as a defensive reflex.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝吃坏了东西，一直在呕吐。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao chī huài le dōngxi, yìzhí zài ǒutù.
examples.english: The baby ate something bad and keeps vomiting.

examples.hanzi: 吃了这种药，有人会感到呕吐。
examples.pinyin: Chī le zhè zhǒng yào, yǒu rén huì gǎndào ǒutù.
examples.english: Some people feel nauseous after taking this medicine.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.
义 (justice, meaning) also lends its sound to 议 yì discuss, 仪 yí ceremony and 蚁 yǐ ant — a useful clue in many characters.

example.hanzi: 这本词典对这个词的定义很清楚。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn cídiǎn duì zhège cí de dìngyì hěn qīngchǔ.
example.english: This dictionary's definition of the word is very clear.
example.fact: The Oxford English Dictionary's first edition took over 70 years to complete, from its initial planning in 1857 to its full publication in 1928, and relied heavily on thousands of volunteer readers who mailed in slips of paper citing how words were actually used in print.

examples.hanzi: 请给“环保”下一个定义。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi “huánbǎo” xià yí ge dìngyì.
examples.english: Please give a definition of “environmental protection”.

examples.hanzi: 不同的人对幸福的定义不一样。
examples.pinyin: Bùtóng de rén duì xìngfú de dìngyì bù yíyàng.
examples.english: Different people define happiness differently.

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand pushing against a cliff 厂: turning back, opposite. Sound series: 饭 fàn, 板 bǎn, 版 bǎn, 返 fǎn.
而 (and, but) — oldest form is a beard (compare 须 xū, beard), later borrowed for the conjunction; 而 survives in 耐 nài.

example.hanzi: 他没有生气,反而笑了起来。
example.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu shēngqì, fǎn'ér xiào le qǐlái.
example.english: He wasn't angry — on the contrary, he started laughing.
example.fact: Placebo treatments in clinical trials sometimes produce real, measurable physiological effects even though the pills contain no active ingredient, an outcome researchers attribute partly to genuine changes in brain chemistry triggered by expectation — a phenomenon robust enough that trial designers must account for it when testing new drugs.

examples.hanzi: 我不但没睡好，反而更累了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ búdàn méi shuì hǎo, fǎn'ér gèng lèi le.
examples.english: Not only did I not sleep well, I'm even more tired.

examples.hanzi: 你这样说，反而让他更难过。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng shuō, fǎn'ér ràng tā gèng nánguò.
examples.english: Saying it like that actually upset him more.

components.note: 彡 (hair strokes, decoration) — patterns and appearance: 形 shape, 影 shadow, 须 beard; 彩 is colorful decoration.
采 (cǎi) sounds exactly like 彩; also in 菜 cài and 踩 cǎi.

example.hanzi: 这场表演很精彩。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng biǎoyǎn hěn jīngcǎi.
example.english: This performance is wonderful.
example.fact: 彩 means color and also splendor: 彩色, 彩虹 (rainbow), 精彩 (wonderful, a common compliment). 彩票 is a lottery ticket, so 中彩 means winning the prize; 彩礼 is the bride price.

examples.hanzi: 天空出现了一道彩虹。
examples.pinyin: Tiānkōng chūxiàn le yí dào cǎihóng.
examples.english: A rainbow appeared in the sky.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们用彩笔画画。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen yòng cǎibǐ huàhuà.
examples.english: The children draw with colored pens.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stones and minerals, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 磨 grind; 碟 is a small plate or dish.
枼 (yè) — close sound: 碟 dié. 枼 also sounds out 蝶 dié and 谍 dié.

example.hanzi: 请给我一个小碟子。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí ge xiǎo diézi.
example.english: Please give me a small dish.
example.fact: 碟 is a small, flat dish: 碟子, 飞碟 (UFO, "flying saucer"), 光碟 (optical disc). The idiom 小菜一碟 means "a piece of cake," literally "one small side dish."

examples.hanzi: 我们点了一碟花生米。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen diǎn le yì dié huāshēngmǐ.
examples.english: We ordered a small dish of peanuts.

examples.hanzi: 他把菜倒进了碟子里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ cài dào jìn le diézi lǐ.
examples.english: He poured the food into the small dish.

components.note: 真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 面对失败,他终于说出了真话。
example.pinyin: miànduì shībài, tā zhōngyú shuōchūle zhēnhuà.
example.english: Facing failure, he finally told the truth.
example.fact: The polygraph, invented in the 1920s, does not actually detect lies — it measures heart rate, blood pressure, and skin conductivity, physiological markers of stress that can spike for many reasons besides deception. That is why U.S. federal courts have generally excluded polygraph results as evidence since the 1923 Frye ruling.

examples.hanzi: 我只想听你说真话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ xiǎng tīng nǐ shuō zhēnhuà.
examples.english: I just want to hear you tell the truth.

examples.hanzi: 小孩子常常会说真话，不会撒谎。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi chángcháng huì shuō zhēnhuà, bú huì sāhuǎng.
examples.english: Little kids often tell the truth and don't lie.

components.note: 子 (child) — 子 means child, as in 孩, 孙; 孤 is a lone child, an orphan.
瓜 (guā) — near sound — 孤 is gū; 瓜 also sounds out 狐 hú and 弧 hú.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.hanzi: 这个慈善机构收养了很多孤儿。
example.pinyin: zhège císhàn jīgòu shōuyǎngle hěn duō gū'ér.
example.english: This charity has adopted many orphans.
example.fact: Kenya's Sheldrick Wildlife Trust runs one of the world's largest elephant orphanages, hand-raising calves whose mothers were killed by poachers or drought. Keepers sleep beside the young elephants at night, because in the wild a calf is almost never out of physical contact with an adult.

examples.hanzi: 他小时候是个孤儿，被奶奶养大。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎoshíhou shì ge gū'ér, bèi nǎinai yǎng dà.
examples.english: He was an orphan as a child and was raised by his grandmother.

examples.hanzi: 志愿者们每个周末都去看望孤儿。
examples.pinyin: Zhìyuànzhěmen měi ge zhōumò dōu qù kànwàng gū'ér.
examples.english: Volunteers visit the orphans every weekend.

components.note: 心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 像 is a person's likeness.
象 (xiàng, elephant) gives the exact sound; 象 first meant elephant, then "image".

example.hanzi: 她想像自己站在舞台中央。
example.pinyin: tā xiǎngxiàng zìjǐ zhàn zài wǔtái zhōngyāng.
example.english: She imagined herself standing at the center of the stage.
example.fact: About 1 in 50 people have aphantasia, a condition in which the mind cannot generate visual images at all — asked to picture a red apple, they report just knowing the concept without any mental picture. The trait was only formally named by neurologist Adam Zeman in 2015, even though it had presumably always existed.

examples.hanzi: 你能想像一下一百年后的世界吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng xiǎngxiàng yíxià yìbǎi nián hòu de shìjiè ma?
examples.english: Can you imagine the world a hundred years from now?

examples.hanzi: 孩子的想像力非常丰富。
examples.pinyin: Háizi de xiǎngxiànglì fēicháng fēngfù.
examples.english: Children have a very rich imagination.

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
巴 (bā) — 巴 gives the sound bā in 爸 bà, 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 疤 bā, so it is a useful sound clue.

example.hanzi: 他摸着下巴思考了很久。
example.pinyin: tā mōzhe xiàba sīkǎole hěn jiǔ.
example.english: He stroked his chin and thought for a long time.
example.fact: The bony chin is a feature unique to Homo sapiens among all primates — even Neanderthals lacked a true chin. Anthropologists still debate why it evolved, with theories ranging from chewing mechanics to a byproduct of the face shrinking as our jaws grew smaller relative to the rest of the skull.

examples.hanzi: 他的下巴上有一道小疤。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xiàba shàng yǒu yí dào xiǎo bā.
examples.english: He has a small scar on his chin.

examples.hanzi: 她把下巴靠在手上，看着窗外。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ xiàba kào zài shǒu shàng, kànzhe chuāngwài.
examples.english: She rested her chin on her hand and looked out of the window.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
氵 (water) — leaking liquid; also in 漏 leak, 流 flow.
世 (shì) is only a loose sound clue for xiè.

example.hanzi: 他靠打拳发泄心中的怒气。
example.pinyin: tā kào dǎquán fāxiè xīnzhōng de nùqì.
example.english: He vents his anger by boxing.
example.fact: For decades, pop psychology claimed that punching a pillow or screaming helps 'let out' anger, but controlled studies by psychologist Brad Bushman in the early 2000s found the opposite: people who vented aggressively afterward became more angry, not less, because the act of venting rehearses and reinforces the aggressive response rather than releasing it.

examples.hanzi: 生气的时候，他喜欢大声唱歌来发泄。
examples.pinyin: Shēngqì de shíhou, tā xǐhuan dàshēng chànggē lái fāxiè.
examples.english: When he's angry, he likes to let off steam by singing loudly.

examples.hanzi: 运动是发泄压力的好办法。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng shì fāxiè yālì de hǎo bànfǎ.
examples.english: Exercise is a good way to release stress.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恐 is fear.
巩 (gǒng) is a near sound match (-ong).
口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 叫, 吗; 吓 is a shout that frightens.
下 (xià) — same sound — 吓 is xià, like 下.

example.hanzi: 他收到了一封恐吓信。
example.pinyin: tā shōudàole yī fēng kǒnghè xìn.
example.english: He received a threatening letter.
example.fact: Rattlesnakes evolved their tail rattle mainly as a bluff — studies show the sound is meant to avoid a costly fight, not to announce an imminent strike. Snakes that are cornered and truly threatened often strike silently instead, saving the rattle for situations where a warning might still let both animals walk away.

examples.hanzi: 不要恐吓小孩子，他们会害怕。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào kǒnghè xiǎo háizi, tāmen huì hàipà.
examples.english: Don't threaten small children, they'll be scared.

examples.hanzi: 他用电话恐吓了邻居。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng diànhuà kǒnghè le línjū.
examples.english: He threatened his neighbor over the phone.

components.note: 彡 (strokes of light or hair) — shining or decoration, as in 形 shape, 彩 colour, 须 beard.
景 (jǐng) is a close sound clue for yǐng; 景 itself meant light; 影 is its shadow.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 像 is a person's likeness.
象 (xiàng, elephant) gives the exact sound; 象 first meant elephant, then "image".

example.hanzi: 医生正在分析X光影像。
example.pinyin: yīshēng zhèngzài fēnxī X guāng yǐngxiàng.
example.english: The doctor is analyzing the X-ray images.
example.fact: In December 1895, physicist Wilhelm Röntgen produced the first X-ray image ever made — a photograph of his wife Anna Bertha's hand, showing her bones and wedding ring in ghostly outline. The discovery earned him the very first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

examples.hanzi: 这张影像非常清楚。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng yǐngxiàng fēicháng qīngchu.
examples.english: This image is very clear.

examples.hanzi: 电脑里保存着孩子成长的影像。
examples.pinyin: Diànnǎo lǐ bǎocún zhe háizi chéngzhǎng de yǐngxiàng.
examples.english: The computer stores footage of the child growing up.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤: clear water.
青 (qīng) gives the exact sound; also 请 qǐng, 情 qíng, 晴 qíng and 精 jīng.
氵 (water) — washing clean; also in 洗 wash, 清 clear.
吉 (jí) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 结 jié.

example.hanzi: 每天早上她都会清洁厨房。
example.pinyin: měitiān zǎoshang tā dūhuì qīngjié chúfáng.
example.english: Every morning she cleans the kitchen.
example.fact: In 1847, Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis discovered that doctors who washed their hands with a chlorinated lime solution before delivering babies cut maternal deaths from childbed fever nearly tenfold. His colleagues mocked the idea, and he died in an asylum years before germ theory finally proved him right.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒店的房间非常清洁。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de fángjiān fēicháng qīngjié.
examples.english: The rooms in this hotel are very clean.

examples.hanzi: 饭前要清洁双手。
examples.pinyin: Fàn qián yào qīngjié shuāngshǒu.
examples.english: You should clean your hands before meals.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.
彳 (step, 双人旁) — walking and paths, as in 行 go, 往 toward; the right half is a sound clue shared with 经 jīng and 劲 jìn.

example.hanzi: 这架望远镜的口径达到了八米。
example.pinyin: zhè jià wàngyuǎnjìng de kǒujìng dádàole bā mǐ.
example.english: This telescope's aperture reaches eight meters.
example.fact: A telescope's resolving power depends almost entirely on its aperture, or 口径 — doubling the diameter of the primary mirror quadruples the light-gathering area. The Extremely Large Telescope under construction in Chile, with a 39-meter mirror built from 798 hexagonal segments, will see roughly 100 million times fainter objects than the naked eye.

examples.hanzi: 这根水管的口径是两厘米。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gēn shuǐguǎn de kǒujìng shì liǎng límǐ.
examples.english: The diameter of this water pipe is two centimeters.

examples.hanzi: 大家要统一口径，不能说法不一样。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā yào tǒngyī kǒujìng, bù néng shuōfǎ bù yíyàng.
examples.english: Everyone should keep to one line and not say different things.

components.note: 童 (child) — as a sound unit, 童 also appears in 瞳 tóng and 撞 zhuàng; the character itself means child, as in 儿童.
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 他常常怀念自己的童年。
example.pinyin: tā chángcháng huáiniàn zìjǐ de tóngnián.
example.english: He often reminisces about his childhood.
example.fact: Historian Philippe Ariès argued in his 1960 book Centuries of Childhood that medieval European societies had little concept of childhood as a distinct stage of life — children were largely treated as small, incompetent adults, and the idea of a protected, separate childhood only solidified in the 17th and 18th centuries.

examples.hanzi: 我的童年是在乡下度过的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tóngnián shì zài xiāngxià dùguò de.
examples.english: I spent my childhood in the countryside.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌让我想起快乐的童年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē ràng wǒ xiǎngqǐ kuàilè de tóngnián.
examples.english: This song reminds me of my happy childhood.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 哈 is the sound of laughing.
合 (hé) — near sound — 哈 is hā; 合 also sounds out 盒 hé.
亻 (person) — Buddha is a person; the same part marks people, as in 仙 immortal, 你 you.
弗 (fú) gives the sound as in 仿佛 fǎng fú; it also sounds out 费 fèi and 拂 fú.

example.hanzi: 他被哈佛大学录取了。
example.pinyin: tā bèi Hāfó dàxué lùqǔle.
example.english: He was admitted to Harvard University.
example.fact: Founded in 1636, Harvard University is the oldest institution of higher education in the United States, established more than a century before the country itself. It takes its name from John Harvard, a young clergyman whose donation of his library and half his estate after his 1638 death was, at the time, one of the largest gifts the fledgling college had received.

examples.hanzi: 哈佛在美国东部。
examples.pinyin: Hāfó zài Měiguó dōngbù.
examples.english: Harvard is in the eastern United States.

examples.hanzi: 她梦想去哈佛读书。
examples.pinyin: Tā mèngxiǎng qù Hāfó dúshū.
examples.english: She dreams of studying at Harvard.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 总 is simplified from 總, whose threads gathered everything together.
衣 (clothing) — cutting cloth to make clothes; also as 衤 in 衬, 被.
戈 (spear) — the cutting blade; also in 战 war, 或 or.

example.hanzi: 这位总裁决定裁员一千人。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi zǒngcái juédìng cáiyuán yī qiān rén.
example.english: This chairman decided to lay off a thousand employees.
example.fact: Kongō Gumi, a Japanese construction firm founded in 578 CE to build Buddhist temples, was run by the same family for over 1,400 years, making it one of the longest continuously operating companies in history before it became a subsidiary of a larger construction group in 2006.

examples.hanzi: 总裁在会议上介绍了新的计划。
examples.pinyin: Zǒngcái zài huìyì shàng jièshào le xīn de jìhuà.
examples.english: The president introduced the new plan at the meeting.

examples.hanzi: 他从小职员做到了公司的总裁。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo zhíyuán zuò dào le gōngsī de zǒngcái.
examples.english: He worked his way up from clerk to president of the company.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — 羞 first meant offering food (a sheep dish) by hand; the sense of shame came later, as in 害羞.
耳 (ear) — ear radical, as in 聪 clever, 聋 deaf, 闻 to hear.
止 (zhǐ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 址 zhǐ and 趾 zhǐ.

example.hanzi: 撒谎后他感到十分羞耻。
example.pinyin: sāhuǎng hòu tā gǎndào shífēn xiūchǐ.
example.english: After lying, he felt deeply ashamed.
example.fact: Charles Darwin devoted an entire chapter of his 1872 book The Expression of the Emotions to blushing, calling it 'the most peculiar and the most human of all expressions.' Blushing is involuntary and visible mainly on the face, and unlike most emotional displays, no other animal is known to do it.

examples.hanzi: 做错事要有羞耻心。
examples.pinyin: Zuò cuò shì yào yǒu xiūchǐxīn.
examples.english: You should have a sense of shame when you do something wrong.

examples.hanzi: 这没有什么可羞耻的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè méiyǒu shénme kě xiūchǐ de.
examples.english: There's nothing to be ashamed of in this.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 折 shows a hand swinging an axe 斤, so to chop or snap, then to fold and bend.
斤 (axe) — 斤 is an axe, as in 析 and 新; it is the cutting tool.

example.hanzi: 这家店的衣服打八折。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de yīfu dǎ bā zhé.
example.english: The clothes in this shop are 20% off.
example.fact: In Chinese discounts, 折 counts what you pay in tenths: 八折 means pay 80%, i.e., 20% off — the opposite of what some learners expect. 折 also means to fold (折纸), to break (折断) and to turn (转折).

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服打了七折。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu dǎ le qī zhé.
examples.english: This piece of clothing is thirty percent off.

examples.hanzi: 她把纸折成了一只小船。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhǐ zhé chéng le yì zhī xiǎochuán.
examples.english: She folded the paper into a little boat.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — the "walk/road" radical appears in characters of going and moving — 过, 进, 送, 逃; here it shows running after something.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 捕 is to seize.
甫 (fǔ) is a loose clue; also in 铺 pù, 辅 fǔ, 薄 báo.

example.hanzi: 警方正在追捕逃犯。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng zhèngzài zhuībǔ táofàn.
example.english: The police are hunting down the escaped criminal.
example.fact: Bloodhounds have roughly 300 million scent receptors, compared to about 6 million in humans, and their tracking ability is considered so reliable that many U.S. courts allow bloodhound-trail evidence in criminal trials — some documented trails have been successfully followed hundreds of hours after a person walked through.

examples.hanzi: 警察追捕小偷，穿过了好几条街。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhuībǔ xiǎotōu, chuānguò le hǎo jǐ tiáo jiē.
examples.english: The police chased the thief through several streets.

examples.hanzi: 这名逃犯被追捕了三个月。
examples.pinyin: Zhè míng táofàn bèi zhuībǔ le sān ge yuè.
examples.english: This fugitive was hunted for three months.

components.note: 尸 (body) — a body with 毛 fur behind it is a tail; 尸 also in 屁, 尿 and 层.
毛 (hair, fur) — the furry tip hanging off the back.
巴 (bā) — 巴 gives the sound bā in 爸 bà, 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 疤 bā, so it is a useful sound clue.

example.hanzi: 小狗高兴地摇着尾巴。
example.pinyin: xiǎo gǒu gāoxìng de yáozhe wěiba.
example.english: The puppy happily wagged its tail.
example.fact: A 2014 study using force-plate treadmills found that kangaroos push off the ground with their tails with as much force as an average human leg produces while walking — effectively making the tail a fifth limb rather than just a tool for balance.

examples.hanzi: 猫的尾巴又长又软。
examples.pinyin: Māo de wěiba yòu cháng yòu ruǎn.
examples.english: The cat's tail is long and soft.

examples.hanzi: 小松鼠有一条毛茸茸的大尾巴。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo sōngshǔ yǒu yì tiáo máoróngróng de dà wěiba.
examples.english: The little squirrel has a big fluffy tail.

components.note: 见 (see) — seeing and looking, as in 现, 觉, 看: 视 is to look.
礻 here is 示 (shì), the altar radical in 礼 and 神: in 视 it is the exact sound clue.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 组; 线 is thread or line.
戋 (jiān) is a loose sound clue; same part in 浅 qiǎn, 钱 qián and 残 cán.

example.hanzi: 一棵大树挡住了我们的视线。
example.pinyin: yī kē dà shù dǎngzhùle wǒmen de shìxiàn.
example.english: A big tree blocked our line of sight.
example.fact: Because light travels in straight lines while Earth's surface curves away beneath it, a ship's lookout standing ten meters above the waterline can only see a lighthouse's beam after cresting the horizon. That is why classic lighthouses were built as tall as possible — extra height extends the line of sight for miles farther out to sea.

examples.hanzi: 飞机飞远了，慢慢消失在我们的视线里。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī fēi yuǎn le, mànmàn xiāoshī zài wǒmen de shìxiàn lǐ.
examples.english: The plane flew away and slowly disappeared from our sight.

examples.hanzi: 他的视线一直停在窗外的鸟身上。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shìxiàn yìzhí tíng zài chuāngwài de niǎo shēn shàng.
examples.english: His gaze stayed on the bird outside the window.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — curtains and tents are cloth; also in 布 cloth, 帽 hat.
长 (zhǎng) gives a close sound; 胀 zhàng shares it and sounds exactly like 帐.
⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — woven covers, as in 笑 smile, 筷 chopsticks.
逢 (féng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 蓬 péng and 缝 féng.

example.hanzi: 我们在山顶搭起了帐篷。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài shāndǐng dāqǐle zhàngpeng.
example.english: We set up a tent on the mountaintop.
example.fact: Mongolian gers (yurts) are engineered so a family can dismantle the entire structure — lattice walls, roof poles, and felt covering — and pack it onto a single camel or cart in under two hours, a design perfected over centuries of seasonal migration across the steppe.

examples.hanzi: 晚上我们睡在帐篷里。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang wǒmen shuì zài zhàngpeng lǐ.
examples.english: At night we sleep in the tent.

examples.hanzi: 下雨前，我们赶紧把帐篷收了起来。
examples.pinyin: Xiàyǔ qián, wǒmen gǎnjǐn bǎ zhàngpeng shōu le qǐlái.
examples.english: Before the rain, we quickly packed up the tent.

meanings: (fig.) a person's established path in life

components.note: 车 (vehicle) — wheel tracks; also in 轮 wheel, 辆 for cars.
九 (jiǔ) is only a loose sound clue for guǐ.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 这颗卫星正沿着固定轨道运行。
example.pinyin: zhè kē wèixīng zhèng yánzhe gùdìng guǐdào yùnxíng.
example.english: This satellite is moving along a fixed orbit.
example.fact: A satellite placed in geostationary orbit, about 35,786 kilometers above the equator, takes exactly 23 hours 56 minutes to complete one loop — matching Earth's rotation so precisely that it appears to hang motionless over the same spot on the ground, which is why satellite dishes never need to move.

examples.hanzi: 火车在轨道上平稳地行驶。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē zài guǐdào shàng píngwěn de xíngshǐ.
examples.english: The train runs smoothly on the track.

examples.hanzi: 事情的发展偏离了原来的轨道。
examples.pinyin: Shìqing de fāzhǎn piānlí le yuánlái de guǐdào.
examples.english: Things have strayed off their original course.
